feedback.problem:
Find the second-degree Taylor polynomial ${P}_{2}(x)$ of $f(x)=\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)$ about $x=\frac{\pi }{4}.$

${P}_{2}(x)=$
{{field-1}}$\,+$
{{field-2}}$(x-\frac{\pi }{4})\,+$
{{field-3}}${(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=\frac{\pi }{4},$ we plug $a=\frac{\pi }{4}$ into the general formula to give

$$
{P}_{2}(x)=f(\frac{\pi }{4})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}){(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}.
$$

So, we need to work out $f(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ and ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & f(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{3}{2} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡(x)} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =3 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)}{{cos}^{3}⁡(x)} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =6\end{aligned}
$$

We now plug the results for $f(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ and ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =\frac{3}{2}+3(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+6\cdot \frac{1}{2}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}+3(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+3{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
